newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Family to release autopsy on Filipino geologist.
newsitem.headline: Family to release autopsy on Filipino geologist.

text.p: The family of the late Filipino geologist Michael de Guzman on Monday promised to make public the results of an investigation into the death of the man who helped discover Indonesia's controversial Busang gold mine.

"Yes we do. We will be the one to release it," de Guzman's brother, Simplicio Jr, told Reuters when asked if the family planned to make public the autopsy by the Philippines National Bureau of Investigation (NBI).

The chief geologist for Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd died last month after falling out of a helicopter taking him to the Busang jungles in Borneo island, where he helped discover what had been touted as the century's biggest gold find.
Bre-X shocked the mining community last month by admitting that there was a possibility the amount of gold at the Busang property had been overstated.
It had earlier put gold reserves at 70.95 million ounces.
Bre-X has a 45-percent stake in Busang, Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc of the United States has 15 percent and Indonesian interests hold the rest.
De Guzman's brother bitterly criticised some foreign media reports about his brother and attacked a newspaper story suggesting the man his family buried last week was not the geologist.

"They (the NBI) will discuss it with us first, all the findings," he said. "After discussing it with us, we will have to decide whether we'll want to make it public. Definitely, we owe it to the public and we will never keep anything from the public. That's what we promised you."
Some Indonesian officials have said de Guzman's death appeared to be a suicide, but his family in Manila have said he was not the kind of man who would take his own life.
Simplicio said the family was still awaiting the results of autopsies carried out by Indonesian and Philippine investigators.
NBI director Santiago Toledo said his agency hoped to finish its investigation this week, but that it would be up to the family to decide whether to make it public.

"The autopsy has been done but there are some examinations still being conducted... Maybe in another two or three days the pathologists will be able to come out with their findings," Toledo told Reuters.
Toledo said the Filipino doctor who examined de Guzman's remains found the body badly mangled but the cause of death could still be determined.
